Subject: Application titled "Recent Advances in Additive Manufacturing for Mechanical and Aerospace
Engineering"
Dear Dr. Jagath Narayana Kamineni,
It is to inform you that your proposal seeking for financial assistance under "Assistance to Professional Bodies &
Seminar / Symposia Scheme" has been considered and recommended for the same. We are now agreed to
provide  Rs 100000/- to meet the expenses related to TA/DA to Young and Senior Indian Scientists and Pre-
Conference printing as partial grant-in-aid to the recommended application.
The grant is only for "Recent Advances in Additive Manufacturing for Mechanical and Aerospace
Engineering" Dated: 16-Aug-2023 to 17-Aug-2023
Kindly submit the required document/ RTGS within 15 days of the receipt of this letter in order to enable us to
process the file for the release of funds. In case, we do not receive the requested document within the provided
time, it would be presumed that you are not interested in this offer and it would be stand withdrawn automatically.
No further correspondence will be entertained thereafter.
You are requested to submit affidavit (Bond) on Rs. 100/- non-judicial stamp paper, in original (by speed /
registered post), scan copy through online is also required to submit (format link-https://serbonline.in/
SERB/AbstractFilePath?FileType=E&FileName=BND_SSY.pdf&PathKey=DOCUMENT_TEMPLATE)
.
Kindly note that, no separate communication by post would be sent to you in this regard and without prior
approval from SERB, convener cannot change the event date, it may not be acceptable. 
With kind regards,

5. Summary of the event (Max. 1000Words): 
 
The DST -SERB sponsored a three day n ational level symposium on 
“NANOSTRUCTURED MATERIALS TO BATTERY AND SUPERCAPACITORS (NM BS-
2023)” was organized by the d epartment of Physics & Chemistry, Sri Venkateswara College of  
Engineering, Tirupati-517507 from 16 th - 18th March 2023. This symposium brought together 
the leading industrialists, experts, and research scholars working in the field of energy storage 
devices such as batteries and supercapacitors to discover new products/ideas and create 
powerful solutions for th e development of eco -friendly and safe futuristic devices. The 
programme enlightened the participants regarding the recent advances in the application of 
nanostructured materials to batteries and supercapacitors. 
On the first day of the NMBS -2023 symposium, the registration process started at 9:15 
AM, followed by the inauguration at 10:30 AM. The Chief Guest, Prof. Vijayamohanan K 
Pillai, Chair of Chemistry and Dean of Research and Development at IISER Tirupati, delivered 
the keynote lecture on the demand f or energy production and storage using nanostructured 
materials in the fourth -coming decade. Session 1 was conducted from 11:30 AM to 1:00 PM, 
where Prof. Vijayamohanan K Pillai gave a lecture on “Nanostructure Materials for Sustainable 
Energy Storage”.

Session 2, from 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM, included a lecture on “Nanostructured Materials 
for Energy Storage Applications” by Dr. D.H. Nagaraju, Professor, Department of Chemistry, 
REVA University, Bengaluru.  Session 3, from 3:45 PM to 5:00 PM, Dr. D.H. Nagaraju  
continued and gave a talk on “Green synthesis of carbon -based materials to EDLC, 
Pseudocapacitor, Hybrid capacitor applications”. Overall, the first day of the symposium 
focused on the application of nanostructured materials in energy storage and featured  lectures 
from prominent speakers in the field. 
On Day 2 of the symposium, in the Session 4, Dr. D. Ebenezer , Manager R&D, from 
Amara Raja Batteries , Tirupati,  spoke about battery safety measures and troubleshooting, 
covering topics such as identifying fl aws in batteries, safety measures, and lithium -ion battery 
troubleshooting. In the Session 5, Dr. Ebenezer extended his talk on lithium -ion battery safety 
measures and common troubleshooting techniques. There was an interact ive session with the 
participants followed by  felicitation to Dr. D. Ebenezer.  In the Session 6, Dr. D. Sridhar , 
Assistant Manager in R&D from Amara Raja Batteries, Tirupati,  spoke about advancements in 
energy storage technologies, discussing the latest developments and innovations in lithium -ion 
batteries, lead -acid batteries, and advanced lead -acid batteries. He emphasized the need to 
improve energy density, cycle life, and safety, reduce costs and env ironmental impact. In 
Session 7, Dr. Sridhar highlighted the challenges and opportunities in the field and discussed the 
need for research on new materials, manufacturing processes, and recycling technologies. There 
was an intera ctive session with the participants and Dr. D. Sridhar was felicitated by the 
Principal. 
On Day 3 of NMBS -2023, there were three sessions:  Session 8 (9:30 AM -11:00 AM): 
Prof. G. Ranga Rao from IIT Madras delivered a talk on "Chalcogenide -based materials fo r 
electrochemical charge storage applications." The session focused on the use of chalcogenides 
in electrochemical energy storage devices.  Session 9 (11:15 AM-1:00 PM): Prof. G. Ranga Rao 
continued his talk on chalcogenide -based materials and discussed rec ent advancements in the 
synthesis and characterization of these materials. The session also covered the performance of 
chalcogenides in different types of energy storage devices.  Session 10 (2:00 PM -4:00 PM):      
Dr. Aravindan V from IISER , Tirupati deliv ered a talk on "Latest R&D Advancements in 
Supercapacitors." Dr. Aravindan discussed the current challenges in supercapacitor technology 
and highlighted the need for new materials and designs to overcome these challenges. He also 
covered the topic of lithium-ion battery recycling in his session. 
 
The valedictory ceremony marked the end of the National Symposium on 
Nanostructured Materials to Battery and Supercapacitors (NMBS -2023), a three -day event that 
aimed to discuss the development of eco -friendly and economical devices with high safety and
